title: Textures
cards/0/body: A texture is an image wrapped onto geometry using UV coordinates. You load it with TextureLoader and put it into the material's map property.
cards/1/title: Why the colors look washed out
cards/1/body:
Regular images (JPG, PNG) store colors in the sRGB color space. Three.js does its lighting math in linear space. If you do not say the texture is sRGB, its colors are read as linear and come out pale and faded.

Only color maps get this flag (map, emissiveMap). Normal and roughness maps are data, so leave them alone.
cards/2/task: The tile should repeat 4×4 and have correct colors.
cards/3/q: repeat = 4, but instead of tiles you get one copy in the corner and stretched stripes. What is wrong?
cards/3/options/0: wrapS and wrapT are set to ClampToEdge; repeating needs RepeatWrapping
cards/3/explain: By default the edges are "clamped": everything outside 0…1 takes the edge pixel.
cards/4/q: Which textures need colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace? Select all that apply.
cards/4/explain: Normals and roughness are numbers, not colors.
cards/5/explain: MirroredRepeatWrapping repeats too, but mirrors every other copy.
cards/7/q: You changed wrapS on a texture that is already on screen, and nothing happened. What do you do?
cards/7/explain: Some texture settings only take effect when the texture is uploaded to the GPU.
